14 A thin horizontal plate of area 0.036 m2 is beneath the surface of a liquid of density 930 kg m–3.
The force on one side of the plate due to the pressure of the liquid is 290 N.
What is the depth of the plate beneath the surface of the liquid?
A
0.88 m
B
1.1 m
C
1.8 m
D
8.7 m

hints: Notice the $290 \text{ N}$ force acts on one side of area $0.036 \text{ m}^2$, so first find the liquid pressure at the plate from $p = F/A$.
Recall hydrostatic pressure in a liquid of density $930 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ varies with depth as $p = \rho g h$.
Rearrange to $h = F/(A \rho g)$ and substitute with $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to compare with the $0.88 \text{ m}$ to $8.7 \text{ m}$ options.
walkthrough: Find the pressure at the plate depth from the given force and area: $p = F/A$.
State the hydrostatic pressure rule for depth $h$ in liquid density $\rho$: $p = \rho g h$.
Rearrange for depth: $h = p/(\rho g) = F/(A \rho g)$.
Substitute $\rho = 930 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $h \approx 8060/(930 \times 9.81) \approx 8060/9123 \approx 0.88 \text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$.

A.explanation: Pressure of about $8060 \text{ Pa}$ divided by $\rho g$ gives $h \approx 0.88 \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: Too large because it does not satisfy $F = \rho g h A$ with $F = 290 \text{ N}$ and $A = 0.036 \text{ m}^2$.

C.explanation: About twice the correct depth, possibly from an error in using area or doubling the force on one side.

D.explanation: Much too large, consistent with omitting $g$ and using $h = F/(\rho A)$.
